syllabusTopics: Introduction: Three domains of life, binomial nomenclature, five kingdom classification system (Monera, Protista, Fungi, Plantae and Animalia)
Status of flora in Nepal and world representation
Fungi: General introduction and characteristic features of phycomycetes, ascomycetes, basidiomycetes and deuteromycetes
Structure and reproduction of Mucor and Yeast
Introduction of Mushrooms, poisonous and non-poisonous mushrooms, economic importance of fungi
Lichen: General introduction, characteristic features and economic importance of lichen
Algae: General introduction and characteristic features of green, brown and red algae; structure and reproduction of Spirogyra; economic importance of algae
Bryophyta: General introduction and characteristic features of liverworts, hornworts and moss; morphological structure and reproduction of Marchantia; economic importance of bryophytes
Pteridophyta: General introduction and characteristic features of pteridophytes; morphological structure and reproduction of Dryopteris; economic importance of pteridophytes
Gymnosperm: General introduction and characteristic features of Gymnosperms; morphology and reproduction of Pinus; economic importance of gymnosperm
Angiosperm: Morphology of root, stem, leaves, inflorescences, flowers and fruit
Taxonomic study: Definition, taxonomic hierarchy, classification systems (artificial, natural and phylogenetic) of angiosperms

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Modern taxonomy classifies life using two complementary systems: the three-domain system (Bacteria, Archaea, Eukarya) based on molecular evidence, and the five-kingdom system (Monera, Protista, Fungi, Plantae, Animalia) based on cell structure and nutrition. The taxonomic hierarchy (Domain → Species) and binomial nomenclature (Genus species) provide universal naming.…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
Taxonomic hierarchy: Domain → Kingdom → Phylum/Division → Class → Order → Family → Genus → Species
Binomial nomenclature: Genus + specific epithet (e.g., Homo sapiens)
Alternation of generations: Sporophyte (2n) → Spores (n) → Gametophyte (n) → Gametes → Zygote (2n)

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Five-kingdom (Whittaker) separates fungi from plants; the older two-kingdom (Linnaeus) placed fungi under plants.  ·  Three-domain and five-kingdom are complementary: domains refer to genetic/cell structure; kingdoms to ecological role.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: NEB expects students to know the five-kingdom system (Whittaker) and the three-domain system (Woese) with their bases of classification.  ·  Taxonomic hierarchy questions are very frequent — memorise all 8 ranks with examples.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: Rhododendron arboreum (Nepal national flower) — Division Magnoliophyta, family Rhododendraceae.  ·  Pinus merkusii — Division Pinophyta, gymnosperm; a common Himalayan conifer.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: In bryophytes, the Gametophyte (n) is the dominant, visible generation; in seed plants the Sporophyte (2n) is dominant.  ·  Pteridophytes have true vascular tissue (xylem + phloem) but no seeds; bryophytes lack true vascular tissue.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: Tabulate 5 kingdoms (cell, nutrition, example)  ·  List 8 taxonomic ranks with examples

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: 5 kingdoms: M-P-F-P-A (Monera, Protista, Fungi, Plantae, Animalia).  ·  3 domains: B-A-E (Bacteria, Archaea, Eukarya).

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: How does the three-domain system differ from the five-kingdom system?  ·  Explain why fungi were separated from plants in the five-kingdom classification.

rows.label: Hints
rows.text: Very frequent: tabulate the five kingdoms (cell type, nutrition, examples).  ·  Explain three-domain system with 16S rRNA evidence.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: Three-domain system  ·  Five-kingdom classification  ·  Taxonomic hierarchy  ·  Binomial nomenclature

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Three domains: Bacteria, Archaea, Eukarya (based on 16S rRNA).  ·  Five kingdoms: Monera, Protista, Fungi, Plantae, Animalia (Whittaker, 1969).  ·  Taxonomic hierarchy: 8 ranks from Domain to Species.  ·  Binomial nomenclature: Genus species (italicised, two-part Latin name).

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Linnaeus named over 7,000 plant and animal species using binomial nomenclature.  ·  Whittaker's five-kingdom system (1969) is still the most widely used teaching classification.

rows.label: More practice
rows.text: What is the significance of the 16S rRNA gene in taxonomy?  ·  Draw the taxonomic hierarchy of a flowering plant (angiosperm) with examples.  ·  Define alternation of generations and give one bryophyte and one angiosperm example.

rows.label: More hints
rows.text: Draw and label the taxonomic hierarchy.  ·  Explain alternation of generations in bryophytes and angiosperms.

rows.label: Extra solved
rows.text: Oryza sativa (rice) — Division Magnoliophyta, family Poaceae; staple food of Nepal.  ·  Marchantia polymorpha — Division Marchantiophyta (liverwort), bryophyte.

rows.label: MCQ drill
rows.text: The five-kingdom classification was proposed by: → C  ·  Fungi are separated from plants in the five-kingdom system because they: → B

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: Three-domain system (Woese, 1977): Bacteria, Archaea, Eukarya — based on 16S rRNA gene sequences.  ·  Five-kingdom classification (Whittaker, 1969): Monera (prokaryotes), Protista, Fungi, Plantae, Animalia — based on cell type and mode of nutrition.  ·  Binomial nomenclature (Linnaeus, 1753): Genus species (italicised, e.g. Rhododendron arboreum).

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Alternation of generations  ·  Plant evolution  ·  Alternation of generations: key feature of all land plants.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Plant evolution: algae → bryophytes → pteridophytes → gymnosperms → angiosperms.  ·  Gymnosperms produce "naked" seeds in cones; angiosperms produce seeds enclosed in fruit.  ·  Binomial nomenclature: always italicise or underline the full scientific name; only the genus is capitalised.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Alternation of generations is a hallmark of Plantae; the dominant generation (gametophyte vs sporophyte) varies by division.  ·  Memorise the 5 kingdoms, their cell type (pro/eukaryotic), nutrition mode, and one example each.  ·  Learn the 8 ranks of the taxonomic hierarchy with a plant and an animal example.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Practice writing scientific names: Rhododendron arboreum, Oryza sativa, Pinus merkusii.  ·  Understand alternation of generations with a labelled cycle diagram.  ·  The three-domain system reorganised all life into three primary lineages based on 16S rRNA sequence analysis.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Whittaker's five-kingdom system remains the most widely used classification in school-level biology.  ·  All land plants undergo alternation of generations between haploid and diploid phases.  ·  The evolution of the flower and seed (angiosperm innovation) made plants the most successful terrestrial group.
